name: גִּלֲלַי
gloss: meaning not given; perhaps “rolled” or “of Galal”
summary: A musician of the priests' line at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, one of the brothers of Zechariah who played “with the instruments of song of David the man of God”, with Ezra the scribe going before them (Neh 12:36). The name is built on the root's consonants with the ending ‑ai, like Milalai beside it; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani, with the instruments of song of David.”

note: The meaning is uncertain; the ‑ai ending may be a short form of a longer name or a gentilic. Milalai and Gilalai stand together in one verse and may be a rhyming pair.
